title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:control}
Let $\lambda\in W^{1,\infty}(0,1)$ and $T_c>0$. For the linearization of \eqref{eq:plant} with the two boundary inputs $U_1=u(0,\cdot)$ and $U_2=u_{xx}(0,\cdot)$, started from $u(\cdot,0)=0$, the set of terminal states \eqref{eq:reachable} reached by controls $(U_1,U_2)\in C_c^\infty((0,T_c);\mathbb R^2)$ is dense in $L^2(0,1)$.

label: prop:obstruction
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:obstruction}
Let $\lambda\in W^{1,\infty}(0,1)$ and let $\mu$ be a double eigenvalue of
$A_{\lambda}$. Consider the linearization of \eqref{eq:plant} actuated through the curvature input only,
$U_1\equiv0$, with any linear feedback $U_2=F(u)$ where $F$ is defined on a subspace of
$L^2(0,1)$ containing $E_\mu$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $\mu$ is an eigenvalue of the closed loop: there is
$\psi\in E_\mu\setminus\{0\}$ with $u(t)=e^{\mu t}\psi$ solving the closed-loop
equations. Thus, no such feedback yields a decay rate larger than $-\mu$, and
none is stabilizing if $\mu\ge0$. The same holds with $U_1$ and $U_2$
exchanged.
\item For constant $\lambda$, $A_{\lambda}$ has a double eigenvalue exactly when
$\lambda=(i^2+j^2)\pi^2\in\mathscr N_\lambda$, and the corresponding double
eigenvalue is $\mu=i^2j^2\pi^4>0$. For every $\lambda\in\mathscr N_\lambda$ the
curvature input alone cannot stabilize the linearized plant.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: One input does not suffice

title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove (i). Since $\dim E_\mu=2$ and $F$ is scalar, choose
$0\ne\psi\in E_\mu\cap\ker F$. Its hinged boundary conditions and
$F(\psi)=0$ satisfy the feedback boundary conditions, so
$u(t)=e^{\mu t}\psi$ remains a closed-loop solution. Thus no decay rate
exceeding $-\mu$ is possible, and $\mu\ge0$ precludes exponential
stability. The argument similarly applies with the inputs interchanged,
completing (i).

For (ii), take constant $\lambda$. Equality of the eigenvalues of distinct sine
modes $i\ne j$ gives $\lambda=(i^2+j^2)\pi^2$ and the positive repeated
eigenvalue $\mu=i^2j^2\pi^4$. Applying (i) proves (ii).

head: environment
name: Kernel and gain exist, and the transformation is invertible

title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove (i). We apply \cite[Prop.~4.1 and Thm.~3.3]{HayatLoko2026} to
$(\mathcal A,B)=(\mathcal A'_{\lambda},B_2)$ with $m=1$, using Theorem~\ref{thm:generic}(ii)
to verify the hypotheses. Condition (H1) of Definition~\ref{def:admissible} gives algebraic simplicity,
and Theorem~\ref{thm:generic}(ii) gives semigroup generation, a Riesz basis,
and the bounds \eqref{eq:HL-hyp}. These verify conditions (6)--(7)
and (13) of that reference with $\alpha=4$, $\beta=-1$, and $\gamma=0$.
Condition (H3) of Definition~\ref{def:admissible} supplies the admissible target shift $a$.

Proposition~4.1 of that reference gives a feedback functional
$\mathcal F$, with coefficients $\mathcal F\chi_n=K_n$, satisfying
\begin{align}
\mathcal F&\in\mathcal L(\mathcal H^{-1/2+\epsilon};\mathbb C),
\qquad (n^{1/2-\epsilon}K_n)_n\in\ell^2,
\qquad \epsilon>0,\label{eq:app-e-display-003}
\end{align}
and a transformation satisfying \eqref{eq:Fequiv-intro}, with
\begin{align}
T:\mathcal H^r&\longrightarrow\;\mathcal H^r
\quad\text{an isomorphism},\qquad -\frac92<r<\frac52.\label{eq:app-e-display-004}
\end{align}
This is the cited range for $\mathcal H^{\beta+r}$, with $\beta=-1$
and $1/2-\alpha<r<\alpha-1/2$. Its equations (50) and (90) give
$TB_2=B_2$ and the intertwining identity in
$\mathcal L(\mathcal H^{1+s},\mathcal H^{-3+s})$ for $|s|<3/2$.
Its Lemma~5.19 gives semigroup generation for the closed-loop operator
$\mathcal A'_{\lambda}+B_2\mathcal F$.

Lemma~5.7 of \cite{HayatLoko2026} gives uniqueness of the feedback
coefficients. It remains to verify the gain regularity.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:spectrum}(ii), $D(\mathcal A'_{\lambda}{}^*)=D(A_{\lambda})$, with graph norm
equivalent to the $H^4$ norm. Interpolating the adjoint eigenvector
synthesis map between $\ell^2\to L^2$ and $\ell^2_4\to H^4$, using the
Riesz and eigenvalue bounds of Theorem~\ref{thm:generic}(ii), gives boundedness
$\ell^2_s\to H^s$ for $0\le s\le4$. Thus
\eqref{eq:app-e-display-003} gives $h\in H^s(0,1)$ for $0\le s<1/2$,
with its series converging in $L^2$.

Uniqueness and the real plant data give a real-valued gain. Together with
the operator identities and semigroup generation above, this proves (i).

We next prove (ii). The isomorphism assertion is \eqref{eq:app-e-display-004}.
Taking $r=0$ in \eqref{eq:app-e-display-004} and using the Riesz-basis
norm equivalence gives bounded invertibility on $L^2(0,1)$, proving (ii).

We next prove (iii). Equations (55), (77), and (83) of
\cite{HayatLoko2026} give the stated spectral formulas. The proof of its Lemma~5.8 gives
$(\kappa_n n^\epsilon)_n\in\ell^2$ for $0<\epsilon<5/2$.

In the Riesz basis, the matrix of $K=I-T$ is
\begin{align}
\hat K_{pn}&=\;\delta_{np}
 +\frac{K_nb_p'}{\mu_n'-\mu_p'+a},
\qquad \hat K_{nn}=-\frac{\kappa_n}{a},\label{eq:app-e-display-007}
\end{align}
where the diagonal identity follows from $K_nb_n'=-(a+\kappa_n)$.
Boundedness of $(\kappa_n)$ and Theorem~\ref{thm:generic}(ii) give
$|K_n|\le Cn^{-1}$ and $|b_p'|\le Cp$. Together with the spectral gaps,
(H3) of Definition~\ref{def:admissible}, and $(\kappa_n)\in\ell^2$, these imply
\begin{align}
\sum_{p,n}|\hat K_{pn}|^2&<\;\infty.\label{eq:app-e-display-009}
\end{align}
Thus $K$ is Hilbert--Schmidt, and the kernel series
\eqref{eq:hk-explicit} converges in $L^2((0,1)^2)$.
Uniqueness and the real plant data make the coefficients conjugate-symmetric,
so conjugate eigenvalue pairs combine to give real $h$ and $k$.
This proves (iii).

Finally, to prove (iv), project \eqref{eq:Fequiv-intro} onto the original plant
eigenbasis, using \eqref{eq:Aprime-modal} and $T=I-K$.
Reversing the computation in Proposition~\ref{prop:modal}, $TB_2=B_2$
gives \eqref{eq:modal-b}, and the intertwining gives \eqref{eq:modal-a}.
Conversely, a solution in the stated class gives the same operator identities,
so uniqueness of the feedback and transformation gives the same modal coefficients.
This proves (iv).

name: Exponential stability of forced target system

title: Proof
body_md:
Theorem~\ref{thm:generic}(ii) supplies the Riesz basis and quartic spectral growth,
while Lemma~\ref{lem:high} shows that sufficiently high eigenvalues are
real and negative. We use these properties to prove (i), then establish
the forced energy identity in (ii) and the decay and forcing estimates in (iii).

We first prove (i). In the Riesz coordinates of Theorem~\ref{thm:generic}(ii),
$J^{-1}(\mathcal A'_{\lambda}-a)J=\operatorname{diag}(\mu_n'-a)$, and the semigroup is
obtained by shifting \eqref{eq:app-d-display-066}. By \eqref{eq:nu},
$\operatorname{Re}(\mu_n'-a)\le-\nu$. Since only finitely many eigenvalues
are nonreal, Lemma~\ref{lem:high} also gives
$|\arg(a-\mu_n')|\le\pi/2-\delta'$ for some $\delta'>0$.
The diagonal semigroup therefore extends analytically to a sector.

To establish existence and regularity in (i), fix a finite interval
$[0,\tau]$ and let
$f\in L^2(0,\tau;\mathcal H^{-2})$. The variation-of-constants formula
gives, in each coordinate,
\begin{align}
w_n(t)&=\;e^{(\mu_n'-a)t}w_{0,n}
 +\int_0^t e^{(\mu_n'-a)(t-s)}f_n(s)\,\mathrm d s.\label{eq:app-f-display-005}
\end{align}
Taking the real part of the coordinate equation after multiplication by
$\overline{w_n}$, applying Young's inequality, and integrating gives
\begin{align}
\int_0^\tau(a-\operatorname{Re}\mu_n')|w_n|^2\,\mathrm d t
&\le\;|w_{0,n}|^2+
\int_0^\tau\frac{|f_n|^2}{a-\operatorname{Re}\mu_n'}\,\mathrm d t.\label{eq:app-f-display-006}
\end{align}
Theorem~\ref{thm:generic}(ii) and the positive margin \eqref{eq:nu} give
$cn^4\le a-\operatorname{Re}\mu_n'\le Cn^4$. Summing therefore gives
$w\in L^2(0,\tau;\mathcal H^2)$ and
$w_t\in L^2(0,\tau;\mathcal H^{-2})$.
Retaining the terminal energy in the same scalar estimate and summing
only over $n>N$ gives
\begin{align}
\sup_{0\le t\le\tau}\sum_{n>N}|w_n(t)|^2
&\le\;\sum_{n>N}|w_{0,n}|^2
+\int_0^\tau\sum_{n>N}\frac{|f_n(s)|^2}{a-\operatorname{Re}\mu_n'}\,\mathrm d s
\longrightarrow0\quad(N\to\infty).\label{eq:target-continuous-tail}
\end{align}
Thus the finite modal sums converge in $C([0,\tau];L^2(0,1))$ to the mild
solution. Uniqueness follows from \eqref{eq:app-f-display-005}.
Since $\tau$ is arbitrary, this proves (i).

We next prove (ii). Each coordinate is absolutely continuous and satisfies, almost everywhere,
\begin{align}
\frac{\,\mathrm d}{\,\mathrm d t}|w_n|^2
&=\;2\operatorname{Re}\big((\mu_n'-a)|w_n|^2+f_n\bar w_n\big).\label{eq:app-f-display-008}
\end{align}
By \eqref{eq:app-f-display-006}, the summed dissipation is integrable.
Moreover, weighted Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\begin{align}
\sum_n|f_n\bar w_n|
&\le\;\|f\|_{\mathcal H^{-2}}\|w\|_{\mathcal H^2}
\in L^1(0,\tau).\label{eq:app-f-display-010}
\end{align}
The integrated identities for the partial sums converge uniformly, and
their derivatives converge in $L^1(0,\tau)$. Thus $V(w)$ is absolutely
continuous and satisfies \eqref{eq:Vdot}.

The weight bounds and the choice of $c_\gamma$ were established in
Section~\ref{ssec:uniform}. Together with \eqref{eq:Vdot}, they complete (ii).

Finally, we prove (iii). For $f=0$, \eqref{eq:app-f-display-005} and
\eqref{eq:nu} give $V(w(t))\le e^{-2\nu t}V(w_0)$.
The norm equivalence \eqref{eq:riesz-const} yields the second estimate
in \eqref{eq:target-decay}. For general $f$, weighted Cauchy--Schwarz
and Young's inequality give
\begin{align}
2\operatorname{Re}\langle f,w\rangle_{\mathcal H}
&\le\;\delta\sum_n\gamma_n|w_n|^2
 +\delta^{-1}\sum_n\frac{|f_n|^2}{\gamma_n},
\qquad \delta>0.\label{eq:app-f-display-014}
\end{align}

Substituting into \eqref{eq:Vdot} for $0<\delta<1$ gives
\eqref{eq:target-forced}. Its norm bound follows from
$\gamma_n\ge c_\gamma n^4$, completing (iii).

label: def:solution
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:solution}
Let $u_0\inL^2(0,1)$ and set
$Y_\tau:=C([0,\tau);L^2(0,1))\cap L^2_{\rm loc}([0,\tau);\mathcal H^2)$.
A function $u\in Y_\tau$ is a \emph{solution} of the closed loop
\eqref{eq:plant}, \eqref{eq:U1}, \eqref{eq:U2hat} on the interval
$[0,\tau)$ if the function $w:=Tu$ is the mild solution of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-mild-solution}
w_t=(\mathcal A'_{\lambda}-a)w+f,\qquad w(0)=Tu_0,
\end{equation}
where $f\in L^2_{\rm loc}([0,\tau);\mathcal H^{-2})$ is the corresponding
target forcing.

label: prop:wp
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:wp}
Consider the Kuramoto--Sivashinsky plant \eqref{eq:plant} with the pre-feedback \eqref{eq:U1} and the perturbed curvature feedback \eqref{eq:U2hat}, that is $U_2=\langle \hat h,u\rangle$. For every $u_0\inL^2(0,1)$ and every $\hat h\inL^2(0,1)$ there is $\tau>0$, depending only on $\|u_0\|$, $\|\hat h-h\|$ and the design, and a unique solution of the closed loop on $[0,\tau)$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:solution}. Any two solutions coincide on their common interval of existence. If $[0,\tau^*)$ is the maximal interval of existence and $\tau^*<\infty$, then $\|u(t)\|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow\tau^*$. Moreover $t\mapsto V(Tu(t))$ is absolutely continuous on compact subsets of $[0,\tau^*)$ and satisfies \eqref{eq:Vdot} with $f$ as in \eqref{eq:target-full}.
